    In Rust, ownership ensures each value has exactly one owner, and borrowing lets you access that value through shared (&T) or mutable (&mut T) references without taking ownership. These rules are enforced at compile time to guarantee memory safety without a garbage collector.

    Overview

    Rust’s memory model is built on ownership, borrowing, and lifetimes. These concepts allow Rust to manage memory safely and efficiently at compile time, avoiding runtime garbage collection. Rust Programming Language

    Ownership

    Rust enforces three core ownership rules:

    • Each value has a single owner.
    • Only one owner exists at a time.
    • When the owner goes out of scope, the value is dropped automatically. ZetCode

    Moves

    Assigning or passing a non-Copy value transfers ownership (a move). After a move, the previous binding becomes invalid.
    Example:

    Rust
    let s1 = String::from("hello");
    let s2 = s1; // move: s1 is now invalid

    Borrowing

    Borrowing allows temporary access to a value without transferring ownership. Rust enforces strict aliasing rules:

    • Shared borrow (&T):
      • Many aliases allowed
      • Read-only access
    • Mutable borrow (&mut T):
      • Only one mutable reference allowed
      • Exclusive read/write access
        ZetCode

    Borrow Checker Rule

    Rust enforces aliasing XOR mutation:

    • You may have many shared borrows, or one mutable borrow, but not both at the same time.
      This prevents data races and ensures safe mutation. YouTube

    Lifetimes

    Lifetimes ensure that references are always valid. They describe how long a borrow lasts and prevent dangling references. Rust usually infers lifetimes automatically. Rust Programming Language

    Stack vs Heap

    • Stack: fixed-size, fast, copied by value (e.g., i32, bool).
    • Heap: dynamically sized data (e.g., String, Vec<T>). Ownership determines who frees heap data. learningrust.org

    ConceptOwnershipAliasingMutabilityAfter Use
    MoveTransferredNo aliasingDepends on new ownerOld binding invalid
    Shared Borrow (&T)Retained by ownerMany aliasesRead-onlyEnds after last use
    Mutable Borrow (&mut T)Retained by ownerExclusive aliasRead/writeEnds after last use
